title: Incremental Rollout Ops Sprintbook — Latency Budgets & KPI Gatekeepers
body:
Purpose:
A compact, actionable sprintbook for incremental feature rollouts (0->100%). Focus is on the intersection of roadmap pacing, latency & cost budgets, and the KPI gatekeepers that stop/slow rollouts. This is intended to live alongside the release checklist but provides the operational levers and signals product-ops and SRE will use during ramps.

Who should use this: product-ops lead (owner), release engineer (exec), SRE oncall, customer-support escalation lead, and the feature PM.

How to use (quick):
- Populate the rollout rows below with the feature and target cohort dates.
- Fill baseline KPIs (pre-rollout steady-state) and define gating thresholds (stop/slow/continue).
- During each ramp day the oncall or release engineer updates the two-line ‘status note’ and toggles traffic or rollback flags.

Sprintbook timeline (example rows — copy into tracker sheet):
- Feature: contextual-search-v2
  - Phase: internal -> alpha -> beta -> gradual -> full
  - Dates: 2025-02-10 -> 2025-02-17 -> 2025-02-24 -> 2025-03-03 -> 2025-03-10
  - Target cohorts: 5% engs, 10% early-adopters, 25% beta, 50% gradual -> 100%
  - Status note (today): canary healthy, p95 latency +8% vs baseline, costs +2%
  - Action: hold at 25%, SRE investigating serialization latency on p2-32s

KPI gatekeepers (definitions and thresholds):
- Latency p95 generation (ms):
  - Baseline: 380ms
  - Continue if <= +5% (<=399ms)
  - Slow down if +5% to +15% (400–437ms) — reduce traffic ramp rate by 50% and open incident chat
  - Stop & rollback if > +15% (>437ms) for >=10m
- Error rate (5xx + client-failure % of requests):
  - Baseline: 0.35%
  - Continue <= 1.0%
  - Slow if 1.0%–2.5% (increase tracing, subset rollbacks)
  - Stop if >2.5% for a sustained 5m window
- Cost per 1k requests (trend compared to baseline):
  - Trigger investigation if > +12%
  - Soft stop if > +25% for sustained 1hr
- Quality regression (eval set A/B):
  - Fail if quality delta > -3% on sentinel prompt set (auto-eval)
  - Soft slow if delta between -1% and -3%

Latency budget matrix (ops knobs):
- Expected host p95 headroom: 15%
- Batching knobs: max_batch_size, target_batch_ms. If p95 rises, reduce target_batch_ms first, then reduce max_batch_size.
- Quantization toggle: can be flipped for private/dedicated customers only — requires preflight regression run.
- Fallback model mapping: fast-variant-01 -> fallback lowest-latency variant. Fallback automatically enabled at stop threshold in routing policy if rollout tagged as 'auto-fallback-eligible'.

Staffing & escalation play (during ramp window):
- Day 0 (canary): Product-ops owner + SRE lead + Release eng + PM + CS rep on 30-min cadence for first 3 hours, then hourly check-ins x6.
- Ramp days: oncall SRE + product-ops on Slack channel #rollout-{feature} and triage conference bridge ready.
- Escalation steps:
  1) Triage in channel 2) If stop threshold hit -> page SRE lead and product director 3) If unresolved +30m escalate to CTO oncall

Canary traffic ramp plan (sample):
- 0% -> 1% (1h) -> 5% (3h) -> 10% (6h) -> 25% (24h) -> 50% (48h) -> 100% (72h)
- Ramp increments only after 30m stable windows where all gatekeepers are green. If any slow condition appears, reduce next increment by 50% and open post-mortem action items.

Contingency toggles (quick reference):
- toggle:route:fallback -> switch routing to fallback-variant across region
- toggle:batching:low-latency -> aggressive small-batch mode (increases CPU but reduces tail latency)
- toggle:kv-cache:flush -> clear KV caches (used rarely; causes short-term latency spike but removes staleness)
- toggle:scale:burst -> temporary burst to dedicated pool (requires reserved capacity approval for >2h)

Preflight checklist (must be completed before canary):
- [ ] Load test script for expected query mix exists (link in linked_artifacts)
- [ ] Auto-eval set ready and baseline metrics recorded
- [ ] Feature flag gate created and tested in staging
- [ ] Rollback playbook validated (documented steps + owners)
- [ ] Alerting thresholds configured in console and verified via synthetic events
- [ ] Tracing/stack sampling at 100% for canary cohort enabled
- [ ] CS & support playbook drafted for customer-impact scenarios

Daily ramp update template (what the release engineer posts to the channel):
- Date/time: 2025-02-24 11:15Z
- Current traffic: 25%
- KPIs: p95=410ms (+7.9%), error=0.9%, cost delta=+1.8%
- Last action: paused ramp, investigating serialization on p2-32s
- Next steps: reduce batch target from 40ms->25ms, re-check in 30m
- Owners: SRE (Marcus), Infra (Jules), PM (Ana)

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Define clear short-form naming standard for rollout channels (should include feature, date, env).
- Validate exact rollback latency impact when toggling route:fallback across regions (sim run needed).
- Add automation: if p95 dropped and error rate >1.5%, automatically throttle model size for new requests (idea only).

Appendix: short links and helpers
- Rollout channel template: #rollout-{feature}-{date}
- Incident bridge template: zoom.us/j/rollout-bridge (use code OPS-RB)
- Quick query for kpi dashboard: p95_generation_last_5m_by_region

Notes to self: keep this sprintbook lean. If a rollout needs >2 pages of special case steps, move to feature-specific runbook under /product-ops/feature-runbooks/.

End of doc.
summary: Compact operational sprintbook for controlled feature rollouts with explicit latency budgets, KPI gates, and staffing/escalation steps. Draft for product-ops and SRE review.
